body_text:
Intermediate value theorem. Let $a<b$ and let
$f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous. If $y$ lies between $f(a)$
and $f(b)$, meaning
$\min\{f(a),f(b)\}\leq y\leq\max\{f(a),f(b)\}$, then there is
$c\in[a,b]$ such that $f(c)=y$. If $y$ lies strictly between the
endpoint values, $c$ may be chosen in $(a,b)$.
